subject.title: Bug: v2026.6.6 apply_patch and write tool fail for paths outside workspace sandbox (/tmp, absolute paths)

question: Should sandboxed `apply_patch` treat a path accepted by the mount-aware filesystem bridge as authorized even when its resolved host path is outside the workspace root?
rationale: The evidence establishes an inconsistency for operator-declared binds, but the exact security contract for bridging a container-authorized path to a host path must be confirmed by the owners of the containment policy.

options.title: Honor bridge-authorized writable mounts
options.body: Remove or narrow the redundant sandbox host-root assertion only after bridge resolution, while preserving bridge path-guard checks and adding mount-focused regression coverage.

options.title: Keep workspace-only semantics strict
options.body: Retain the current rejection and document that `apply_patch` intentionally excludes explicit binds, accepting divergence from sandboxed `write` and `edit`.

options.title: Design a separate opt-in policy
options.body: Add a clearly scoped setting only if maintainers decide configured Docker binds must not themselves establish apply-patch authority.

recommendation.title: Honor bridge-authorized writable mounts
recommendation.body: Remove or narrow the redundant sandbox host-root assertion only after bridge resolution, while preserving bridge path-guard checks and adding mount-focused regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history shows repeated ownership of the workspace-containment and sandbox-path security boundary.
